steps.name: environment
steps.description: Prepare a safe, idempotent headless environment. Compute npm global bin at setup time (validate it is a directory and inside a safe prefix), write a workspace-scoped /etc/profile.d fragment that only exports PATH augmentation and CI when the shell PWD is inside the workspace to avoid changing global behavior for unrelated users, and write a workspace-local .env.agent.sh that agents can source immediately (contains CI=true and PATH augmentation). Validate node and npm presence and versions; emit clear remediation guidance if versions are insufficient. Do not run npm at shell startup. Operates in the workspace path.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
PROFILE_D="/etc/profile.d/simple_calculator_env.sh"
AGENT_ENV="$WORKSPACE/.env.agent.sh"
NPM_GBIN=""
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  NPM_GBIN=$(npm --silent bin -g 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
# Validate computed npm global bin: must be non-empty and an absolute existing dir under /usr or /home
if [ -n "${NPM_GBIN}" ] && [ -d "${NPM_GBIN}" ]; then
  case "${NPM_GBIN}" in
    /usr/*|/home/*|/opt/*) SAFE_NPM_GBIN="${NPM_GBIN}" ;;
    *) SAFE_NPM_GBIN="" ;;
  esac
else
  SAFE_NPM_GBIN=""
fi
# Write system-wide profile fragment but scope it to the workspace to avoid surprising global effect
sudo bash -c "cat > '${PROFILE_D}' <<EOF
# SimpleCalculatorApplication global env fragment (only active when PWD inside workspace)
# This file appends workspace-local npm global bin and CI when shells are inside the workspace.
if [ -n \"\${PWD-}\" ] && printf '%s' "\"\${PWD}\"" | grep -q "^${WORKSPACE}"; then
  export CI=true
  $( [ -n "${SAFE_NPM_GBIN}" ] && printf 'PATH=%s:\$PATH\nexport PATH' "${SAFE_NPM_GBIN}" || printf '')
fi
EOF"
sudo chmod 644 "${PROFILE_D}"
# Workspace-local env for immediate agent use (always safe for agent-run tasks)
cat > "${AGENT_ENV}" <<EOF
# Workspace-local env for SimpleCalculatorApplication (sourced by agent tasks)
export CI=true
$( [ -n "${SAFE_NPM_GBIN}" ] && printf 'export PATH="%s:$PATH"\n' "${SAFE_NPM_GBIN}" || printf '' )
EOF
chmod 644 "${AGENT_ENV}"
# Validate node/npm presence and versions, but provide remediation guidance rather than silent failures
if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: node and npm must be available on PATH. Image lists nodejs/npm; ensure they are present." >&2
  exit 2
fi
NODE_V_RAW=$(node -v 2>/dev/null || true)
NODE_V=$(printf "%s" "${NODE_V_RAW}" | sed 's/^v//' | cut -d- -f1)
NPM_V=$(npm -v 2>/dev/null || true)
NODE_MAJOR=$(printf "%s" "${NODE_V}" | cut -d. -f1 || echo 0)
NPM_MAJOR=$(printf "%s" "${NPM_V}" | cut -d. -f1 || echo 0)
if [ "${NODE_MAJOR}" -lt 16 ]; then
  echo "WARNING: Node >=16 recommended (found ${NODE_V_RAW}). Consider updating Node in the container or using an image with Node >=16." >&2
  exit 3
fi
if [ "${NPM_MAJOR}" -lt 8 ]; then
  echo "WARNING: npm >=8 recommended (found ${NPM_V}). Consider updating npm." >&2
  exit 4
fi
# Source workspace-local env for current session (non-fatal)
[ -f "${AGENT_ENV}" ] && . "${AGENT_ENV}" || true

steps.name: install dependencies
steps.description: Install project-local dependencies non-interactively using npm. Ensure devDependencies are installed even in CI/headless mode by temporarily unsetting NODE_ENV=production and using npm ci / npm i with --include=dev. Use package-lock.json + npm ci when present; otherwise run npm i --include=dev to generate package-lock.json. Redirect logs to /tmp for diagnostics and verify local binaries node_modules/.bin/vite and node_modules/.bin/vitest exist. Operates in the workspace path.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
LOG=/tmp/simple_calculator_npm_install.log
# Ensure devDependencies are installed even with CI=true by unsetting NODE_ENV if set to production
OLD_NODE_ENV="${NODE_ENV-}"
if [ "${OLD_NODE_ENV}" = "production" ]; then
  unset NODE_ENV
fi
# Use npm ci when package-lock.json exists; include dev deps explicitly
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --include=dev >"${LOG}" 2>&1 || { cat "${LOG}" >&2; exit 4; }
else
  npm i --no-audit --no-fund --include=dev >"${LOG}" 2>&1 || { cat "${LOG}" >&2; exit 5; }
fi
# restore NODE_ENV
[ -n "${OLD_NODE_ENV}" ] && export NODE_ENV="${OLD_NODE_ENV}" || true
# Verify expected local binaries
[ -x node_modules/.bin/vite ] || { echo "ERROR: vite binary missing" >&2; tail -n 200 "${LOG}" >&2 || true; exit 6; }
[ -x node_modules/.bin/vitest ] || { echo "ERROR: vitest binary missing" >&2; tail -n 200 "${LOG}" >&2 || true; exit 7; }
[ -d node_modules ] || { echo "ERROR: node_modules not present" >&2; exit 8; }

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Build the Vite app, start a preview server from local node_modules/.bin/vite, poll until HTTP responds, capture evidence (status code, headers, snippet of body) into /tmp, then stop the server cleanly. Add trap-based cleanup, verify preview binary before launching, fix evidence path handling, and use robust readiness polling with timeout. Operates in the workspace path and sets CI=true for reproducible build behavior.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export CI=true
BUILD_LOG=/tmp/simple_calculator_build.log
PREVIEW_LOG=/tmp/simple_calculator_preview.log
EVIDENCE_PREFIX="/tmp/simple_calculator_evidence"
PORT=5173
# Build using local vite binary
if [ -x node_modules/.bin/vite ]; then
  ./node_modules/.bin/vite build >"${BUILD_LOG}" 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: build failed" >&2; tail -n 200 "${BUILD_LOG}" >&2; exit 12; }
else
  npm run build >"${BUILD_LOG}" 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: build failed (npm script)" >&2; tail -n 200 "${BUILD_LOG}" >&2; exit 13; }
fi
# Verify preview binary
if [ -x node_modules/.bin/vite ]; then
  PREVIEW_CMD=("./node_modules/.bin/vite" "preview" "--port" "${PORT}")
else
  echo "ERROR: preview binary missing" >&2
  exit 14
fi
# Start preview in background and capture PID
"${PREVIEW_CMD[@]}" >"${PREVIEW_LOG}" 2>&1 &
PREVIEW_PID=$!
# Ensure cleanup
trap 'if [ -n "${PREVIEW_PID:-}" ]; then kill "${PREVIEW_PID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi' EXIT
# Wait for server to become responsive (up to 60s)
TRIES=0
MAX_TRIES=60
OK=0
while [ ${TRIES} -lt ${MAX_TRIES} ]; do
  if curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^2'; then
    OK=1; break
  fi
  sleep 1
  TRIES=$((TRIES+1))
done
if [ "${OK}" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: preview server did not respond after ${MAX_TRIES}s" >&2
  tail -n 200 "${PREVIEW_LOG}" >&2 || true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Validation: build, preview, readiness poll, capture evidence, cleanup
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "${WORKSPACE}"
export CI=true

BUILD_LOG="/tmp/simple_calculator_build.log"
PREVIEW_LOG="/tmp/simple_calculator_preview.log"
EVIDENCE_PREFIX="/tmp/simple_calculator_evidence"
STATUS_FILE="/tmp/simple_calculator_status.txt"
PORT=5173
READINESS_TIMEOUT=60

# Ensure evidence directory (prefix uses /tmp so nothing to create beyond confirming)
: > "${BUILD_LOG}"
: > "${PREVIEW_LOG}"

# Build using local vite binary if available, otherwise fallback to npm run build
if [ -x "${WORKSPACE}/node_modules/.bin/vite" ]; then
  "${WORKSPACE}/node_modules/.bin/vite" build >"${BUILD_LOG}" 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: build failed, see ${BUILD_LOG}" >&2; tail -n 200 "${BUILD_LOG}" >&2; exit 12; }
else
  # Try npm run build (assumes script exists)
  npm run build >"${BUILD_LOG}" 2>&1 || { echo "ERROR: build failed (npm run build), see ${BUILD_LOG}" >&2; tail -n 200 "${BUILD_LOG}" >&2; exit 13; }
fi

# Verify preview binary
PREVIEW_BIN="${WORKSPACE}/node_modules/.bin/vite"
if [ ! -x "${PREVIEW_BIN}" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: preview binary missing at ${PREVIEW_BIN}" >&2
  exit 14
fi

# Prepare to start preview
PREVIEW_CMD=("${PREVIEW_BIN}" preview "--port" "${PORT}" "--strictPort")

# Start preview in background and capture PID
"${PREVIEW_CMD[@]}" >"${PREVIEW_LOG}" 2>&1 &
PREVIEW_PID=$!

# Trap-based cleanup to ensure preview is stopped
_cleanup() {
  rc=$?
  if [ -n "${PREVIEW_PID:-}" ]; then
    kill "${PREVIEW_PID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    wait "${PREVIEW_PID}" 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
  exit ${rc}
}
trap _cleanup EXIT

# Poll for HTTP readiness
start_time=$(date +%s)
end_time=$((start_time + READINESS_TIMEOUT))
ready=0
while [ $(date +%s) -le ${end_time} ]; do
  # Use curl with low timeouts to avoid hangs
  http_code=$(curl -sS --max-time 2 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" || true)
  case "${http_code}" in
    2??|3??)
      ready=1; break;;
    *)
      sleep 1;;
  esac
done

if [ "${ready}" -ne 1 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: preview server did not respond with 2xx/3xx within ${READINESS_TIMEOUT}s" >&2
  echo "--- last ${PREVIEW_LOG} ---" >&2
  tail -n 200 "${PREVIEW_LOG}" >&2 || true
  exit 15
fi

# Capture evidence reliably using the prefix
EVIDENCE_HEADERS="${EVIDENCE_PREFIX}_headers.txt"
EVIDENCE_BODY="${EVIDENCE_PREFIX}_body.html"
EVIDENCE_SUMMARY="${EVIDENCE_PREFIX}_summary.txt"
EVIDENCE_SNIPPET="${EVIDENCE_PREFIX}_snippet.html"

# Fetch headers and body (with timeouts)
curl -sS --max-time 5 -D "${EVIDENCE_HEADERS}" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" -o "${EVIDENCE_BODY}" 2>/dev/null || true
STATUS=$(curl -sS --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:${PORT}/" || echo "000")

echo "status:${STATUS}" > "${EVIDENCE_SUMMARY}"
# Append first portion of headers to summary
if [ -f "${EVIDENCE_HEADERS}" ]; then
  head -n 200 "${EVIDENCE_HEADERS}" >> "${EVIDENCE_SUMMARY}" || true
fi
# Create a short snippet of body
if [ -f "${EVIDENCE_BODY}" ]; then
  head -n 50 "${EVIDENCE_BODY}" > "${EVIDENCE_SNIPPET}" || true
fi

# Mark success
echo "validation_success" > "${STATUS_FILE}"

# Cleanup: kill preview if still running (trap will also handle)
if ps -p "${PREVIEW_PID}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  kill "${PREVIEW_PID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  wait "${PREVIEW_PID}" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Remove trap and exit 0
trap - EXIT
exit 0
